message.content:
**How to kill Visual Studio Code (code.exe) from the command line**

On Windows you can terminate a running program with the built‑in `taskkill` utility.  
Below are the most common ways to stop VS Code (`code.exe`) safely.

---

### 1. Kill by image name (recommended)

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM` – specifies the image name (process name).  
* `/F` – forces termination (equivalent to “End Task” in Task Manager).

This will close *all* instances of `code.exe` that are currently running.

---

### 2. Kill by process ID (PID)

If you only want to close a specific instance:

1. Find the PID(s):

   ```cmd
   tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
   ```

   Example output:

   ```
   Image Name                     PID Session Name        Session#    Mem Usage
   ========================= ======== ================ =========== ============
   code.exe                   12345 Console                    1     150,000 K
   ```

2. Terminate that particular PID:

   ```cmd
   taskkill /PID 12345 /F
   ```

---

### 3. Using PowerShell (alternative)

PowerShell offers a more readable syntax:

```powershell
Get-Process code | Stop-Process -Force
```

or to target a specific PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id 12345 -Force
```

---

### 4. Things to keep in mind

| Issue | What to watch out for |
|-------|------------------------|
| **Multiple VS Code windows** | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` will close *every* VS Code window. If you only want to close one, use the PID method. |
| **Administrator rights** | Usually not required for terminating your own processes, but if VS Code was launched with elevated privileges, you may need to run the command prompt as Administrator. |
| **Unsaved work** | `taskkill /F` forces the process to exit immediately, so any unsaved files will be lost. Use with caution. |
| **Background services** | VS Code may spawn helper processes (`code-helper.exe`, `code.exe` for extensions, etc.). Killing the main `code.exe` will usually terminate the whole application, but if you see other helper processes lingering, you can target them similarly. |

---

### Quick cheat‑sheet

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Force‑close all VS Code windows |
| `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"` | List all VS Code processes with their PIDs |
| `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` | Force‑close a specific VS Code instance |
| `Get-Process code | Stop-Process -Force` | PowerShell equivalent of the first command |
| `Stop-Process -Id <pid> -Force` | PowerShell equivalent of the PID command |

---

#### Example session

```cmd
C:\> tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
Image Name                     PID Session Name        Session#    Mem Usage
========================= ======== ================ =========== ============
code.exe                   5678 Console                    1     120,000 K
code.exe                   9012 Console                    1     115,000 K

C:\> taskkill /PID 5678 /F
SUCCESS: Sent termination signal to process ID 5678.

C:\> taskkill /IM code.exe /F
SUCCESS: Sent termination signal to process ID 9012.
```

That’s it! Use the method that best fits your situation.
